summary: LLM inference costs can be reduced by 50–95% through a combination of caching, model routing, prompt compression, and output constraints — without sacrificing quality. Research from 2026 shows prompt caching alone cuts API costs 41–80%, while combining it with batch APIs and model routing can push total savings past 90%. These optimizations matter most at scale: a chatbot handling 1M conversations/month on a flagship model costs ~$3,250/month, but smart routing and caching can drop that to under $500.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse previously computed KV cache for repeated prompt prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples, long documents). Providers charge a fraction of normal input token rates for cache hits. Anthropic offers a 90% discount on cached tokens; OpenAI and Google offer similar discounts. Works best when prompts share a long static prefix across many requests.
techniques.savings: 41–90% reduction in input token costs on cached portions
techniques.example: Place your 2,000-token system prompt and static few-shot examples at the top of every request with cache_control enabled in Anthropic's API; subsequent requests hitting that prefix cost 90% less per cached token, reducing a $3,000/month bill to ~$300 for the cached portion.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache LLM responses by semantic similarity of the input query, not just exact string match. When a new query is semantically close to a cached one (e.g., cosine similarity > 0.95), return the cached response without calling the API at all. Achieves cache hit rates of 40–60% in production workloads with repeated or paraphrased queries.
techniques.savings: 40–60% reduction in total API calls; up to 45% cache hit rate reported in production
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache with a sentence-transformer embedding model; queries like 'What are your business hours?' and 'When are you open?' resolve to the same cached response, eliminating the second API call entirely.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Classify incoming requests by complexity and route them to the cheapest model that can handle them adequately. Simple classification, extraction, and FAQ tasks go to budget models ($0.15–$0.60/M tokens); complex reasoning or generation goes to flagship models ($2–15/M tokens). A typical routing split of 70% budget / 25% mid-tier / 5% flagship yields large aggregate savings.
techniques.savings: 50–80% reduction in average cost per request
techniques.example: Use LiteLLM with a router config that sends intent classification to GPT-3.5/Haiku and only escalates to GPT-4/Claude Opus when a confidence score or task-complexity classifier flags a hard query — routing 70% of traffic to the cheap tier cuts average cost from $2.50/M to ~$0.60/M tokens.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduce the number of input tokens by removing redundant phrasing, compressing few-shot examples, trimming system prompts to under 200 tokens, and using structured schemas instead of verbose format instructions. Tools like LLMLingua perform learned compression that preserves semantic content while cutting token count 30–50%.
techniques.savings: 20–50% reduction in input tokens; direct proportional cost reduction
techniques.example: Replace a 600-token verbose system prompt with a 180-token structured version using bullet points and remove filler phrases like 'Please make sure to always remember to' — a 30% prompt reduction translates directly to a 30% drop in input costs across all calls.

techniques.name: Output Constraints (max_tokens + Structured Output)
techniques.description: Set explicit max_tokens limits on API calls to prevent runaway long responses, and use structured output schemas (JSON mode, tool-calling, response_format) to eliminate verbose natural-language framing around the answer. Output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens, making this disproportionately impactful.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and response_format={type:'json_object'} for a product classification task; instead of a 400-token essay-style answer, the model returns a 40-token JSON object, cutting output costs by ~90% on that call.

techniques.name: Batch API Processing
techniques.description: Submit non-latency-sensitive requests as asynchronous batches rather than real-time API calls. OpenAI and Anthropic both offer 50% discounts on batch API calls that accept up to 24-hour turnaround. Ideal for evaluation runs, bulk data processing, embeddings, and offline enrichment pipelines.
techniques.example: Run nightly document summarization jobs using Anthropic's Batch API instead of real-time calls; a pipeline that cost $200/day drops to $100/day with zero code changes beyond switching the API endpoint and adding a result-polling step.

techniques.name: Quantization and Right-Sizing (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: For self-hosted or on-premises deployments, use quantized model weights (FP8, INT4) and select the smallest model that meets quality requirements. FP8 quantization on Hopper GPUs is the 2026 gold standard, providing ~30% speed improvements with minimal quality loss. Right-sizing to a 7B or 13B model instead of 70B+ can cut GPU cost 5–10x.
techniques.example: Deploy Llama-3-8B with FP8 quantization on vLLM with continuous batching enabled; for a customer support use case that previously used GPT-4 at $10/M output tokens, this reduces marginal inference cost to ~$0.20/M tokens equivalent at the GPU level.

techniques.name: Continuous Batching and KV Cache Reuse (Self-Hosted Runtime)
techniques.description: At the inference server level, enable continuous batching (dynamic batching of in-flight requests) and prefix KV cache reuse. These system-level optimizations improve GPU throughput 40–80% and can yield up to 23x throughput improvement over naive sequential serving, reducing cost per request at scale.
techniques.savings: 40–80% throughput improvement; 40–60% cost per request reduction at scale
techniques.example: Configure vLLM with enable_prefix_caching=True and set gpu_memory_utilization=0.90; for a workload where all requests share a 1,000-token system prompt, the cached KV state is reused across requests, cutting time-to-first-token by up to 31% and improving throughput by 2–3x.

techniques.name: Context Window Management and Summarization
techniques.description: Trim conversation history by summarizing older turns instead of passing the full context, and remove irrelevant retrieved documents before sending to the LLM. Long contexts are expensive due to the quadratic attention cost and per-token pricing. Tools like LangChain's ConversationSummaryMemory automate this.
techniques.savings: 20–60% input token reduction on multi-turn or RAG workloads
techniques.example: In a 20-turn chatbot, summarize turns 1–15 into a 200-token summary and only pass the last 5 turns verbatim; this keeps context under 1,000 tokens instead of ballooning to 4,000+, reducing input costs by up to 75% on long sessions.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy and SDK that routes requests across 100+ LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, etc.) with load balancing, fallbacks, cost tracking, and model routing rules. Acts as a drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source (free); LiteLLM Enterprise with SSO/RBAC from ~$500/month

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM APIs. Embeds queries and stores responses; on cache hit returns stored response without API call. Supports multiple backends (Redis, FAISS, Milvus) and embedding models. Integrates with LangChain and LlamaIndex.
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source; infrastructure costs only

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Redis Stack or Redis Cloud with vector search for semantic caching of LLM responses. LangChain's RedisSemanticCache uses Redis as the backend for embedding-based response caching with configurable similarity thresholds.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud from $0 (30MB free) to usage-based enterprise pricing; Redis Stack self-hosted is free

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost management proxy. Logs all API calls, tracks spend by model/user/feature, surfaces expensive prompts, and offers caching and rate limiting. One-line integration by changing the base URL.
tools.pricing_paid: Free up to 100K requests/month; Growth at $20/month; Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM applications with built-in support for semantic caching (RedisSemanticCache, InMemoryCache), conversation summary memory, model switching, and prompt templating to reduce token usage.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source (free); LangSmith observability platform from $39/month

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine for self-hosted LLMs. Implements PagedAttention, continuous batching, FP8 quantization, prefix caching, and tensor parallelism. Dominates production self-hosted deployments in 2026.
tools.pricing_paid: Fully open source; GPU infrastructure costs only

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft Research tool for prompt compression using a small language model to identify and remove low-information tokens from prompts while preserving semantic meaning. Achieves 2–5x compression ratios with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with semantic caching, model fallbacks, load balancing, and spend analytics. Supports 200+ LLMs via a unified API. Provides detailed cost breakdowns and automated routing based on latency and cost targets.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; Growth from $49/month; Enterprise custom

tools.name: Prem AI
tools.description: Platform with built-in prompt caching, model routing, and cost optimization across providers. Includes semantic caching with configurable similarity thresholds and detailed per-request cost attribution.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Pro and Enterprise tiers available

tools.name: OpenMeter
tools.description: Usage metering and billing infrastructure for AI applications. Tracks token consumption per user/feature/model, enabling accurate cost attribution and budget alerts to prevent runaway spend.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source self-hosted (free); Cloud from $0 with usage-based pricing

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching on Anthropic or OpenAI for any system prompt longer than 1,024 tokens — zero code change beyond adding a cache_control header, and saves 41–90% on those input tokens immediately.

Set explicit max_tokens limits and switch to JSON/structured output mode on all API calls that return structured data — output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens, so cutting response length by 50% has outsized impact.
Move all non-real-time workloads (batch summarization, evaluations, data enrichment) to the Batch API (OpenAI or Anthropic) for an automatic 50% cost reduction with no quality tradeoff.

Add a model router that sends simple tasks (classification, extraction, FAQ) to a budget model like GPT-3.5 or Claude Haiku ($0.25–$1/M tokens) instead of a flagship model — even a 70/30 split saves 50–70% on average cost per request.

Audit and compress your system prompts to under 200 tokens by removing filler phrases and switching from verbose instructions to structured bullet points — a 30% reduction in average prompt length directly cuts input costs by 30% across every single API call.
